lab_claim: CDK definition of a private RDS PostgreSQL instance (publiclyAccessible=false; isolated subnets; storage, Performance Insights and generated secret encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key; IAM authentication; SG-to-SG ingress only). Synthesized and unit-tested offline.
limitations: Never deployed. No database accounts, default-account handling, password rotation or activity monitoring were exercised against a running database. Tests assert template properties only.
organizational_dependencies: DBA role and accountability; data classification of what the database holds; access request/approval and periodic access recertification; password and privileged-account standards; database activity monitoring and review staffing.

lab_claim: Changes are proposed as pull requests from feature branches; a credential-free GitHub Actions workflow (tsc, jest, cdk synth, cdk-nag gate, evidence hash check) ran on PR #1 and its run records were captured; a separate written review of PR #1/#2 exists.
limitations: All six PRs are still open; nothing has been merged to main, so no approved change has reached the baseline. Single author/operator. Branch protection, required reviewers and approval records were not verified. CI runs are of lab code, not of a production change.
organizational_dependencies: Change management policy and change categories; change advisory/approval authority; segregation of duties between author, approver and deployer; emergency change procedure; post-implementation review; change records retention.

lab_claim: Reference design choices that relate to resilience: RDS Multi-AZ and deletion protection, S3 versioning and RETAIN removal policies. Synthesized offline; cross-region replication is explicitly a proposed exception (EX-02).
limitations: No failover, AZ loss or recovery test was performed. No cross-region or cross-account copy. Not integrated with any business continuity program. Exception EX-02 is PROPOSED, not approved.
organizational_dependencies: Business continuity management program; business impact analysis with RTO/RPO; resilience testing schedule and lessons-learned process; exception approval authority; third-party (CSP) resilience due diligence.

lab_claim: Offline Entra ID Conditional Access baseline that blocks legacy authentication (CA001), requires MFA (CA002) and blocks Microsoft admin portals from untrusted locations for privileged roles (CA007); a fail-closed validator ran against the baseline and against negative/malformed fixtures.
limitations: Synthetic fixtures only; no Entra tenant or Microsoft Graph was used, so nothing describes a real tenant's state. No VPN, remote desktop, third-party or customer remote access paths exist in the lab.
organizational_dependencies: Remote access policy and approved methods; named-location (trusted network) ownership; third-party remote access agreements; break-glass account custody and review; licensing for Conditional Access features.

lab_claim: CDK VPC with PRIVATE_ISOLATED subnets only (no IGW/NAT/public subnets), restricted default security group, app/db security groups without 0.0.0.0/0, and VPC flow logs to a KMS-encrypted log group. Synthesized and unit-tested offline.
limitations: Never deployed; no traffic, routing or reachability was observed. Isolated subnets mean no ingress or egress path for an application has been designed yet. No firewalls, IDS/IPS, DNS or load balancers are modelled.
organizational_dependencies: Network architecture ownership; network diagram and segmentation/trust-level standard; firewall rule review process; network monitoring staffing; connectivity agreements with providers.

lab_claim: Open source dependencies are pinned through committed package-lock.json files; an ADR records the decision to pin cdk-nag 2.x; parliament findings are gated through a documented allowlist with sources.
limitations: No software composition analysis, license review or vulnerability scan of dependencies was run (npm ci is invoked with --no-audit in the recorded commands). No inventory of approved open source components.

lab_claim: Credential-free AWS Organizations reference: OU layout and service control policies (e.g., region lock, deny leaving the organization) exported to JSON, linted and unit-tested; synthesized offline.
limitations: Never applied to any AWS Organization. The offline SCP evaluator is not AWS's policy engine (stated in evidence/orgs/README.md). No ITAM inventory exists to anchor boundaries to real assets.
organizational_dependencies: Definition of system authorization boundaries tied to an IT asset inventory; account/OU ownership; approval authority for SCP changes; validation in a sandbox organization before adoption.

lab_claim: Offline Conditional Access policies requiring MFA for all users and phishing-resistant MFA for privileged roles, with break-glass exclusions enforced by the validator; an SCP denying root-user actions; KMS key policies built by a least-privilege helper with tests for no wildcard principals.
limitations: Synthetic identities and fixtures; no tenant, no AWS account, no real users. Joiner/mover/leaver, access reviews and privileged access management are not modelled.
organizational_dependencies: IAM policy and standards; identity lifecycle tied to HR events; periodic access recertification; privileged access approval and monitoring; break-glass procedures and custody.

lab_claim: Infrastructure is defined as code; configuration baselines are checked by cdk-nag (AwsSolutions and NIST 800-53 R5 rule packs), static guards and negative-control tests; suppressions are limited to a register of proposed exceptions; evidence bundles carry SHA256SUMS.
limitations: Checks evaluate synthesized templates, not deployed resources; no drift detection. The four exceptions (EX-01..EX-04) are PROPOSED and unapproved. Rule packs are tool checks, not an approved institutional baseline.
organizational_dependencies: Configuration management policy; approved secure configuration baselines; exception/risk-acceptance authority; drift monitoring and remediation ownership.

aio_title: Backup and Replication Processes (logical Postgres backup/restore exercise)
lab_claim: A scripted pg_dump/pg_restore exercise with fingerprint comparison and negative tests (truncated dump, garbage archive, missing database, FK enforcement, restore over existing objects, tamper detection) ran in GitHub Actions run 40741329107 against an ephemeral PostgreSQL service container and offline, with PASS results and a verifier. An earlier failing run is preserved and marked historical/invalid.
limitations: Synthetic seed data on ephemeral CI/sandbox databases; not a production system or backup media. Dumps are gitignored; the CI copies live only in workflow artifacts with limited retention, so ARTIFACTS.sha256 cannot be re-verified from the repo alone. No backup schedule, media inventory, off-site copy or encryption of dumps is exercised.
organizational_dependencies: Backup policy and methodology per system criticality; backup schedules and adherence monitoring; media inventory, off-site storage and access controls; restore testing cadence and sign-off; validation of CSP-performed backups.

aio_title: Backup and Replication Processes (AWS-native RDS backups)
lab_claim: An AWS Backup plan (CMK-encrypted vault, daily rule) and RDS automated backup retention of 14 days are defined in CDK and appear in the synthesized template.
limitations: No backup job, snapshot or restore has ever run: the stack was never deployed. EX-04 (AWS-managed backup service-role policy) is PROPOSED. A separate backup/aws work-in-progress directory seen in another local checkout is uncommitted and is not referenced here.
organizational_dependencies: Same as AIO-10, plus AWS account ownership, vault access policy approval, and evidence of periodic restore tests from AWS Backup.

lab_claim: Reference log sources: S3 server access logging into a terminal log bucket that does not log to itself (ADR-0004), VPC flow logs and RDS log exports to KMS-encrypted CloudWatch log groups with 1-year retention, and an organization CloudTrail (multi-region, global service events, log file validation, KMS). Synthesized and nag-checked offline.
limitations: No logs were generated, collected, reviewed or retained because nothing was deployed. No log analysis, alerting, SIEM or review procedure exists. Retention values are lab choices, not an approved retention schedule.
organizational_dependencies: Log management policy and retention schedule (including legal/regulatory retention); log review staffing and escalation; SIEM/monitoring tooling; protection of log integrity and access to logs.

lab_claim: Delegated-admin reference stack for GuardDuty (detector with protection plans) and Security Hub (FSBP and CIS 3.0.0 standards, finding aggregator, central configuration). Synthesized and unit-tested offline; known coverage gaps documented in ADR-0002.

lab_claim: Cloud access-control guardrails expressed as SCPs (protect security services, require encryption, deny public S3) and admin-portal location restriction in Conditional Access; SCPs exported, linted in-repo and with parliament (gated, allowlisted with sources).
limitations: Guardrails were never attached to a real organization or tenant. Linting is static; parliament raw output had 2 findings allowlisted as false positives. The shared-responsibility split with the CSP is not documented in the repo.

lab_claim: Vendor-risk templates (assessment, RACI), a filled example for a fictional vendor, a core-banking vendor outage escalation tabletop scenario, and a governance lint (one Accountable per RACI row, required sections, contract placeholders, no invented vendor SLA numbers) that ran with positive and negative cases offline.
